IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.claim: The Madyan episode displays virtues that prepared Moses for revelation: generosity, helping the distressed, compassion, modesty, gratitude, chastity, and fidelity; Shuaib likewise shows hospitality, protection of the fearful, and gentleness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.anchor: هو ما تضمنته من فضائل الأعمال ومناقب أهل الكمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.claim: These character traits could lead Meccan polytheists to compare Moses with Muhammad's known virtue before his mission and recognize the signs of revelation; Muslims should also emulate prophetic character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.anchor: ليعتبر المشركون بذلك إن كان لهم اعتبار في مقايسة تلك الأحوال بأجناسها من أحوال النبي

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r2.claim: When leaving Egypt Moses had no destination or contact in mind; he turned toward Madyan trusting God to guide him to the right place.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r2.anchor: he had not ascertained his destination

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r3.claim: This was unlike the migration after prophethood, whose timing and stages God determines; Moses had no such guidance here, so his trust models how truth-seekers can be guided without clear promises.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r3.anchor: did not have any such guidance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r1.claim: Tawajjaha means he turned his face; tilqaʾ means toward the direction he faced, and the verbal noun is used adverbially.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r1.anchor: توجه: رد وجهه. وتلقاء: تقدم الكلام عليه في يونس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r2.claim: A report says three roads lay before Moses: he took the middle, pursuers took the others, and he went barefoot and hungry for eight nights, eating leaves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r2.anchor: فأخذ موسى أوسطها، وأخذ طالبوه في الآخرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r3.claim: The apparent sense is that Moses did not know the route and asked God to guide him directly to safety; Ibn Abbas says God brought him to Midian as he walked without knowing the way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r3.anchor: والظاهر من قوله: عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل، أنه كان لا يعرف الطريق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r4.claim: Other reports say Gabriel or another angel guided Moses, or he deliberately chose a safe road that happened to lead to Midian; Mujahid identifies it as the Midian road, Hasan as the path of guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p296/r4.anchor: وقيل: هداه جبريل إلى مدين. وقيل: ملك غيره

FARRA:v2p303#2/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p303#2/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p303#2/r9.claim: Moses headed for the water of Midian; Midian is indeclinable because it is the name of a town.
FARRA:v2p303#2/r9.anchor: مدين لم تصرف لأنها اسم لتلك البلدة.

FARRA:v2p303#2/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p303#2/r10.speaker: الشاعر
FARRA:v2p303#2/r10.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses Madian without declension, illustrating the town name’s grammatical treatment.
FARRA:v2p303#2/r10.anchor:
وقال الشاعر
رهبان مدين لو رأوك تنزلوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

THALABI:v7p243/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p243/r1.claim: The town of Madyan is named after Madyan, son of Ibrāhīm, just as Madāʾin is named after his brother Madāʾin b. Ibrāhīm.
THALABI:v7p243/r1.anchor: وهو مدين بن إبراهيم نسبت البلدة إليه كما نسبت مدائن إلى أخيه مدائن بن إبراهيم

THALABI:v7p243/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p243/r2.claim: Moses did not know the route to Madyan, so he prayed for guidance; an angel then led him there on horseback with a spear.
THALABI:v7p243/r2.anchor: قصد الطريق إلى مدين، وإنما قال ذلك لأنه لم يكن يعرف الطريق إليها، فلما دعا جاءه ملك على فرس بيده عنزة فانطلق به إلى مدين

THALABI:v7p243/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243/r3.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v7p243/r3.claim: The commentators say Moses left Egypt without provisions, money, a mount, or shoes; the journey was eight nights, roughly the distance from Kufa to Basra, and he ate tree leaves.
THALABI:v7p243/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: خرج موسى من مصر بلا زاد ولا درهم ولا ظهر ولا حذاء إلى مدين وبينهما مسيرة ثماني ليال نحوا من الكوفة إلى البصرة

THALABI:v7p243/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p243/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
THALABI:v7p243/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr says Moses left Egypt barefoot and reached Madyan with his soles worn through.
THALABI:v7p243/r4.anchor: قال ابن جبير: خرج من مصر حافيا، فما وصل إلى مدين حتى وقع خف قدميه

ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r1.claim: Madyan, biblical Midian, was inhabited by Amorite Arabs closely related to Hebrews, so its people could help Moses.
ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r1.anchor: The inhabitants of Madyan (called Midian in the Bible) were Arabs of the Amorite group. Since they were racially and linguistically closely related to the Hebrews, they could be counted upon to help Moses in his plight.

ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r2.claim: Asad refers to note 67 on 7:67 for Madyan's geographical location.
ASAD-NOTES:28:22#n20/r2.anchor: For the geographical location of the region of Madyan, see surah 7, note 67.

NASHR:v2p89/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p89/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p89/r1.claim: The original hāʾ in توجه is not imāla: unlike an alif, it has no yāʾ origin; pronoun hāʾ likewise is not inclined, and the preceding consonant is already kasra.
NASHR:v2p89/r1.anchor: الهاء الأصلية نحو (ولما توجه) لا يجوز إمالتها

NASHR:v2p89/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p89/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p89/r2.claim: Imāla is not used for forms such as الصلاة and الزكاة, since inclining their alif would require inclining the consonant before it too.
NASHR:v2p89/r2.anchor: لا تجوز الإمالة في نحو: الصلاة، والزكاة. وبابه مما قبله ألف

NASHR:v2p89/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p89/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p89/r3.claim: Forms such as التوراة and مزجاة allow imāla because their alif derives from yāʾ, not because their hāʾ marks femininity.
NASHR:v2p89/r3.anchor: فلهذا أميلت الألف في نحو: التوراة، ومزجاة. وبابه مما تقدم، لأنها منقلبة عن الياء

NASHR:v2p89/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p89/r4.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p89/r4.claim: Al-Dānī analyzes imāla in these forms as applying to the alif and preceding letter, not the hāʾ, which explains its use in both connected and paused reading.
NASHR:v2p89/r4.anchor: إن الألف وما قبلها هو الممال في هذه الكلمات لا الهاء، وما قبلها إذ لو كان ذلك لما جازت الإمالة فيها في حال الوصل

NASHR:v2p89/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p89/r5.speaker: الداني ومكي
NASHR:v2p89/r5.claim: On al-Dānī’s account, imāla-coloring reaches hāʾ after an inclined fatḥa; this consequence is unnecessary for Makkī’s view that hāʾ itself is never inclined.
NASHR:v2p89/r5.anchor: القدر الذي يحصل في صوت الهاء من التكيف الذي يسمونه إمالة

QIRAAT-ER:28:22:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:22:8#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:28:22:8#1/r1.claim: The possessive yāʾ is pronounced with fatḥa in rabbiya rather than silent or elided rabbī; meaning and morphology remain unchanged.
QIRAAT-ER:28:22:8#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Canonical seven variant: yāʾ of 1cs possessive pronounced with fatḥa (rabbiya)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the middle or straight path as the intended route.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ سواء السبيل ﴾ قال قصد السبيل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r1.claim: Moses turned his face toward Midian; tilqāʾ means the direction opposite or facing it and is originally a verbal noun used adverbially.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r1.anchor: أي صرف وجهه ( تلقاء مدين ( أي ما يقابل جانبها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r2.claim: Midian is Shuʿayb's town, named for Midian son of Abraham; it lay outside Pharaoh's dominion, which explains Moses's choice.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r2.anchor: ومدين قرية شعيب سميت باسم مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام ولم يكن في سلطان فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r3.claim: Other explanations say Moses headed there because he knew the place or because he was related to its people; the journey from Egypt was eight days.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r3.anchor: وقيل توجه اليها لمعرفته به وقيل لقرابته منه عليهما السلام وكان بينها وبين مصر مسيرة ثمان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r4.claim: The straight middle of the road is the route leading to safety.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r4.anchor: أي وسط الطريق المؤدي إلى النجاة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r5.claim: Moses spoke from reliance on God and confidence in His good guidance, while unfamiliar with the routes.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r5.anchor: وإنما قال عليه السلام ذلك توكلا على الله تعالى وثقة بحسن توفيقه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r6.claim: An unattributed report says three roads lay ahead: Moses took the middle, while pursuers chose the other two; he remained barefoot for eight nights, eating only leaves.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r6.anchor: فعن ثلاث طرائق فاخذ الوسطى وأخذ طالبوه في الأخريين وقالوا : المريب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that Moses did not arrive until the coverings of his feet had fallen away.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r7.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير أنه عليه السلام لم يصل حتى سقط خف قدميه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r8.claim: Another report says Gabriel guided Moses to Midian after he set out without knowing the way.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r8.anchor: وروي أن ه عليه السلام أخذ يمشي من غير معرفة فهداه جبريل عليه السلام إلى مدين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r9.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddī says Moses took side paths and met an angel on horseback with a spear; after Moses bowed in fear, the angel told him to follow and led him to Midian.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59#2/r9.anchor: وعن السدي أنه عليه السلام أخذ في بنيات الطريق فجاء ملك على فرس بيده عنزة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says four roads appeared to Moses and he did not know which to take, so he prayed for guidance and took the road to Midian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله عز وجل : ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال : عرضت لموسى اربعة طرق فلم يدر ايتها يسلك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r2.claim: Qatada explains Midian as a watering place belonging to the people of Shuʿayb.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ولما توجه تلقاء مدين ومدين ماء كان عليه قوم شعيب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says the right path was the road to Midian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد عسى ربي ان يهديني سواء السبيل الطريق إلى مدين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the phrase as the straight road and says Moses and a man from Shuʿayb's people, the two best on earth then, met that day.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن يقول : عسى ربي ان يهديني سواء السبيل قال : الطريق المستقيم ، قال : فالتقى والله يومئذ خير اهل الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī explains the phrase as the middle of the road.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي في قوله : عسى ربي اين يهديني سواء السبيل قال : وسط الطريق

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r6.claim: Qatada glosses the right path as the intended or direct road.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قال : عسى ربي ان يهديني سواء السبيل اي قصد السبيل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī reports that an angel led Moses along the path until he reached Midian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960#2/r7.anchor: عن السدي قال موسى وهو متوجه إلى مدين : عسى ربي ان يهديني سواء السبيل قال : فانطلق به الملك حتى انتهى إلى مدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r1.claim: Moses’s migration resembles Abraham’s declaration that he was migrating to his Lord; God guided Moses toward Midian, where he would meet a prophet to teach him prophetic conduct, though Moses did not know his destination or whom he would meet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r1.anchor: هذه هجرة نبوية تشبه هجرة إبراهيم عليه السلام إذ قال { إني مهاجر إلى ربي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r2.claim: The clause about setting out toward Midian coordinates with omitted narrative: after leaving the city and wandering, Moses happened onto a road leading to Midian and prayed for guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r2.anchor: فقوله تعالى { ولما توجه تلقاء مدين } عطف على جمل محذوفة إذ التقدير : ولما خرج من المدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Moses set out without knowing the road, relying only on good expectation of his Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : خرج موسى ولا علم له بالطريق إلا حسن ظن بربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r4.claim: Tawajjaha means to turn one’s face, hence to set one’s course toward Midian.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r4.anchor: و { توجه } : ولى وجهه ، أي استقبل بسيره تلقاء مدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r5.claim: Tilqāʾ is an uncommon verbal noun meaning meeting or proximity; it became a place adverb, here ‘toward the place facing Midian.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r5.anchor: و { تلقاء } : أصله مصدر على وزن التفعال بكسر التاء ، وليس له نظير في كسر التاء إلا تمثال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r6.claim: Midian was a people descended from Midian, son of Abraham.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r6.anchor: و { مدين } : قوم من ذرية مدين بن إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r7.claim: Midian lay on the Red Sea’s western shore; from Rameses or Memphis Moses likely traveled southwest through Amalekite, Edomite, and Nabataean lands, about 850 miles or 45 days on foot, sleeping outdoors but staying on course.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p97/r7.anchor: تلك مسافة ثمانمائة وخمسين ميلا تقريبا . وإذ قد كان موسى في سيره ذلك راجلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r1.claim: Sawāʾ is a straight, untwisted course; the prayer implicitly asks God to guide Moses into the true religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p98/r1.anchor: والسواء : المستقيم النهج الذي لا التواء فيه . وقد ألهمه الله هذه الدعوة التي في طيها

BURSEVI:v6p286/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286/r1.claim: A lover approaching God by way of trial fears that misguided people will obstruct arrival; fear accompanies the seeker until the goal is reached, so he prays for arrival.
BURSEVI:v6p286/r1.anchor: فإذا أقبل العاشق من طريق الامتحان إلى الحق خاف وترقب أن يلحقه أحد من أهل الضلال

BURSEVI:v6p286/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286/r2.claim: Tawajjaha means turning one's face in a direction; tilqāʾ is a verbal noun used as an adverb meaning toward or opposite.
BURSEVI:v6p286/r2.anchor: التوجه (روى باخيري كردن) والتلقاء تفعال من لقيت وهو مصدر اتسع فيه فاستعمل ظرفا

BURSEVI:v6p286/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286/r3.claim: Midian was Shuayb's village by the Red Sea, named for Midian son of Abraham and Keturah, who settled there; it lay outside Pharaoh's domain and eight days from Egypt.
BURSEVI:v6p286/r3.anchor: ومدين قرية شعيب عليه السلام على بحر القلزم سميت باسم مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام من امرأته قنطورا

BURSEVI:v6p286/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286/r4.claim: The verse means Moses turned his face toward Midian and headed toward its vicinity.
BURSEVI:v6p286/r4.anchor: والمعنى لما جعل موسى وجهه نحو مدين وصار متوجها إلى جانبها

BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r1.claim: Moses speaks in trust and good expectation of God, though he does not know the roads.
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r1.anchor: (باخود كفتت) توكلا على الله وحسن ظن به وكان لا يعرف الطرق

BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r2.claim: Sawāʾ al-sabīl means the middle, straight road; a sabīl is a route customarily traveled.
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r2.anchor: وسطه ومستقيمه والسبيل من الطرق ما هو معتاد السلوك

BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r3.claim: Three routes appeared; Moses took the middle one. His pursuers searched the other routes, thinking a fox would avoid the middle, and failed to find him.
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r3.anchor: فظهر له ثلاث طرق فأخذ الوسطى وجاء الطلاب عقبيه فقالوا : إن الفار لا يأخذ الطريق الوسط

BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r4.claim: Although Moses' face was toward Midian, his heart was turned toward God, making the journey a path of longing for encounter.
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r4.anchor: فرموده كه روى مبارك بناحيه مدين داشت أمادلش متوجه بحضرت ذو المدين بود

BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r5.claim: Some interpret Midian as the realm of pre-eternity and post-eternity; Moses sensed reality's breath there and turned toward it for vision and encounter.
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : مدين إشارة إلى عالم الأزل والأبد فوجد موسى نسيم الحقيقة من جانبها

BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r6.claim: The saying about finding the Breath of the Merciful from Yemen is read as sensing truth's breeze from Uways al-Qarani's heart; saintly lands and meetings bring blessings.
BURSEVI:v6p286#2/r6.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : "إني لأجد نفس الرحمن من قبل اليمن" مخبرا عن وجدان نسيم الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r1.claim: Ibn al-Nahhas’s appeal to a report from Ibn Umar as proof that Quranic pause marks are obligatory is unclear; he refers readers to al-Suyuti’s al-Itqan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r1.anchor: النحاس من الاحتجاج لوجوب ضبط أوقاف القرآن بكلام لعبد الله بن عمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r2.claim: They prioritized verse endings, whose challenge to the eloquent leaders among their people established the Quran’s proof against both those leaders and ordinary people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r2.anchor: فكان الاعتبار بفواصله التي هي مقاطع آياته عندهم أهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r3.claim: As many ordinary Arabs and people from other nations entered Islam, scholars marked pauses to ease reading; they applied interpretive criteria, so a marker’s placement conveyed a proposed meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r3.anchor: فلما كثر الداخلون في الإسلام من دهماء العرب ومن عموم بقية الأمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r4.claim: Notable authorities on pause marking include Ibn al-Anbari, Ibn al-Nahhas, al-Nakzawi (or al-Nakzwi), and the later Moroccan scholar Muhammad ibn Abi Jum‘a al-Hibti, who died in 930 AH.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p84/r4.anchor: وأشهر من تصدى لضبط الوقوف أبو محمد بن الانباري ، وأبو جعفر بن النحاس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r7.speaker: ابن الجزري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says no place in the Quran has a universally obligatory or forbidden stop; pause categories are graded by meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r7.anchor: وعلى جميع التقادير لا تجد في القرآن مكانا يجب الوقف فيه ولا يحرم الوقف فيه كما قال ابن الجزري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r8.claim: Stops are classified as emphatic, good, or lesser according to the meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r8.anchor: ولكن الوقف ينقسم إلى أكيد حسن ودونه وكل ذلك تقسيم بحسب المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r9.claim: Some scholars prefer stopping at completed speech and using a shorter pause when meaning calls for a break before completion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r9.anchor: وبعضهم استحسن أن يكون الوقف عند نهاية الكلام وأن يكون ما يتطلب المعنى الوقف عليه قبل تمام المعنى سكتا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r1.claim: Fleeing alone, barefoot, without provisions and unsure of the way, Moses entrusted himself to God; his words show knowledge of God and His gifts of wisdom and knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r1.anchor: ولما خرج موسى عليه السلام فارا بنفسه منفردا حافيا لا شيء معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r2.claim: Tawajjaha means he turned his face toward it; tilqaʾ means toward the direction where the named place lies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r2.anchor: وتوجه، رد وجهه إليها، وتلقاء معناه ناحية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r3.claim: Sawaʾ al-sabil means its middle and its sound, straight course.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r4.claim: At this point God sent the guiding angel mentioned earlier.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r4.anchor: وفي هذا الوقت بعث الله تعالى الملك المسدد حسبما ذكرناه قبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the straight way as the road to Midian.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أراد ب سواء السبيل طريق مدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282#2/r6.claim: Hasan identifies it as the path of guidance.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls Hasan's sense, the way of guidance, more excellent and compares Abu Bakr's description of the Prophet as one who guides him to the path.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p283/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا أبدع ونظيره قول الصديق عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses it as toward Midian; the word derives from liqāʾ, with tāʾ added.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي تجاه مدين ونحوها وأصله اللقاء وزيدت فيه التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r2.claim: The quoted line uses talqāʾik to mean meeting, witnessing the lexical sense from liqāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r2.anchor: أملت خيرك هل تأتي مواعده فاليوم قصر عن تلقائك الامل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r3.claim: Moses set out frightened, without provisions or a mount, on a route of eight days from Egypt to Midian that he did not know; he asked God to guide him to his destination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون خرج خائفا بغير زاد ولا ظهر وكان بين مصر ومدين مسيرة ثمانية أيام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses knew no route and had only good expectation of his Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس لم يكن له علم بالطريق إلا حسن ظنه بربه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says God sent an angel to guide Moses.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي بعث الله له ملكا فدله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r6.claim: The commentators say Moses had no food on his journey but leaves; severe hunger showed through his belly, and he arrived at Midian's water where the herders gathered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211#2/r6.anchor: ولم يكن له في طريقه طعام إلا ورق الشجر فورد ماء مدين وخضرة البقل تتراءى في بطنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r1.claim: Tلقاء means toward; Midian is Shuayb's village, named for Midyan son of Abraham, outside Pharaoh's rule and eight days from Egypt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r1.anchor: { تلقاء مدين } قصدها ونحوها . ومدين : قرية شعيب عليه السلام ، سميت بمدين بن إبراهيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r2.claim: Midian was not under Pharaoh's authority and lay an eight-day journey from Egypt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r2.anchor: ولم تكن في سلطان فرعون ، وبينها وبين مصر مسيرة ثمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses left without knowing the route, relying only on his good expectation of God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : خرج وليس له علم بالطريق إلا حسن ظنه بربه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r4.claim: The straight way is its middle and the main course of the route.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r4.anchor: و { سواء السبيل } وسطه ومعظم نهجه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r5.claim: An unnamed report says Moses went barefoot, lived on leaves, and wore away the sole of a foot before arriving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : خرج حافيا لا يعيش إلا بورق الشجر ، فما وصل حتى سقط خف قدمه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r6.claim: Another report says an angel on horseback, carrying a spear, guided Moses to Midian.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p404#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : جاءه ملك على فرس بيده عنزة ، فانطلق به إلى مدين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r1.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r1.claim: Ikrimah says four roads appeared to Moses and he did not know which one to take.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة : عرضت لموسى أربع طرق فلم يدر أيتها يسلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r2.claim: Ikrimah says Moses prayed this when the roads diverged, then took the road to Midian.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أنه قال ذلك عند استواء الطرق فأخذ طريق مدين , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r3.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi say Moses had already taken the road to Midian and asked to be guided straight along it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r3.anchor: بعد أن اتخذ طريق مدين فقال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل أي قصد الطريق إلى مدين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r4.claim: Qatada identifies Midian as a watering place where Shuayb’s people lived.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p244#3/r4.anchor: قال قتادة : مدين ماء كان عليه قوم شعيب

MUJAHID:v2p482#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p482#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p482#2/r1.claim: The right way Moses hoped to be guided to was the road to Midian.
MUJAHID:v2p482#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل ﴾ قال يعني الطريق إلى مدين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r1.claim: Tilaqaa means toward; tawajjuh is turning toward something.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r2.claim: Midian is Shuayb's town, named after Midian son of Abraham; it lay outside Pharaoh's realm, eight days from Egypt.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r2.anchor: ومدين قرية شعيب عليه السلام سميت بمدين بن إبراهيم ولم تكن في سلطان فرعون وبينها وبين مصر مسيرة ثمانية أيام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses left without knowing the road, relying on good expectation of his Lord.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما خرج ولم يكن له علم بالطريق إلا حسن الظن بربه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r4.claim: Moses asks for the middle and main road; an angel came and led him to Midian.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#4/r4.anchor: أي وسطه ومعظم نهجه فجاء ملك فانطلق به إلى مدين

RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses did not set out for Midian but surrendered himself to God and walked without knowing where he was going until God brought him there.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r1.anchor: إنه خرج وما قصد مدين ولكنه سلم نفسه إلى الله تعالى وأخذ يمشي من غير معرفة

RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r2.claim: Others say Moses intended Midian because he thought its people were related to him through Midian son of Abraham, though he did not know the route and relied on God.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون لما خرج قصد مدين لأنه وقع في نفسه أن بينهم وبينه قرابة

RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r3.claim: Another view says Gabriel came and showed Moses the way to Midian.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r3.anchor: من الناس من قال بل جاءه جبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r4.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from al-Suddī that an angel on horseback met Moses; Moses prostrated in joy, the angel stopped him, and Moses followed toward Midian.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r4.anchor: ذكر ابن جرير عن السدي لما أخذ موسى عليه السلام في المسير جاءه ملك على فرس فسجد له موسى من الفرح

RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r5.claim: Rāzī prefers that Moses meant to reach Midian but did not know the route: “toward Midian,” rather than “to Midian,” and his plea for guidance show uncertainty about the way, not the destination.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r5.anchor: والأقرب أن يقال إنه قصد الذهاب إلى مدين وما كان عالما بالطريق

RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses left Egypt for Midian without provisions or a mount; the journey took eight days and he ate only leaves.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204/r6.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق خرج من مصر إلى مدين بغير زاد ولا ظهر

RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r1.claim: Moses’ plea resembles Abraham’s “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me”; Rāzī says Moses often echoes Abraham in argument, reply, prayer, and supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v24p204#2/r1.anchor: فهو نظير قول جده إبراهيم عليه السلام

STUDYQURAN:28:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r1.claim: Some say Moses did not know the route to Midian and relied on God's benevolence to guide him.
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r1.anchor: Some say that Moses did not know how to get to Midian

STUDYQURAN:28:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r2.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r2.claim: It is said that Moses had no provisions or money.
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r2.anchor: he had no provisions or money (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:22/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r3.claim: R says Moses had no specific destination and trusted only in God.
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r3.anchor: he did not even have a specific destination, but only trusted in God (R)

STUDYQURAN:28:22/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r4.claim: Midian is the land of Shuʿayb's people.
STUDYQURAN:28:22/r4.anchor: Midian was the land of the people of Shuʿayb

TAB-FULL:v18p203/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r1.claim: Moses set his face toward Midian, leaving Pharaoh’s city and authority behind.
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r1.anchor: ولم يصرف اسم مدين لأنها اسم بلدة معروفة، كذلك تفعل العرب بأسماء البلاد المعروفة

TAB-FULL:v18p203/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r2.claim: تلقاء means toward; the expression can also mean from oneself or directly opposite, as in one house facing another.
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r2.anchor: ويقال: داره تلقاء دار فلان: إذا كانت محاذيتها

TAB-FULL:v18p203/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r3.claim: مدين is left indeclinable here as a known town name, following the Arabic treatment of familiar place names.
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r3.anchor: ولم يصرف اسم مدين لأنها اسم بلدة معروفة، كذلك تفعل العرب بأسماء البلاد المعروفة

TAB-FULL:v18p203/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r4.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r4.claim: The poet’s line “رهبان مدين” supplies an example of the town name’s use.
TAB-FULL:v18p203/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [البحر الكامل] رهبان مدين لو رأوك تنزلوا … والعصم من شعف العقول الفادر

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r1.claim: Moses hoped God would show him the direct route to Midian because he did not know the way.

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says an angel found Moses when he was lost among the paths and guided him toward Midian; Moses first prostrated from fear, and the angel told him to follow instead.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " لما أخذ موسى في بنيات الطريق جاءه ملك على فرس بيده عنزة

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses knew no route toward Midian and relied only on his good expectation of God.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " خرج موسى متوجها نحو مدين، وليس له علم بالطريق إلا حسن ظنه بربه

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God prepared the road; Moses left Egypt without food, shoes, mount, money, or bread, fearful until he reached the people at Midian.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " ذكر لي أنه خرج وهو يقول: {رب نجني من القوم الظالمين} [القصص: 21] فهيأ الله الطريق إلى مدين، فخرج من مصر بلا زاد

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the journey from Egypt to Midian took eight days, about the distance from Kufa to Basra; Moses ate leaves, traveled barefoot, and wore away his feet.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " خرج موسى من مصر إلى مدين، وبينها وبينها مسيرة ثمان، قال: وكان يقال نحو من الكوفة إلى البصرة، ولم يكن له طعام إلا ورق الشجر

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas also describes the distance to Midian as eight nights, comparable to the distance from Basra to Kufa.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما خرج موسى من مصر إلى مدين، وبينه وبينها ثمان ليال، كان يقال: نحو من البصرة إلى الكوفة

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r7.claim: Midian was inhabited at that time by the people of Shuʿayb.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r7.anchor: ومدين كان بها يومئذ قوم شعيب عليه السلام

TAB-FULL:v18p204/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r8.claim: Qatada identifies Midian as a watering place inhabited by the people of Shuʿayb.
TAB-FULL:v18p204/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {ولما توجه تلقاء مدين} [القصص: 22] ومدين ماء كان عليه قوم شعيب

TAB-FULL:v18p205/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as the road to Midian.
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: " {سواء السبيل} [البقرة: 108] قال: الطريق إلى مدين

TAB-FULL:v18p205/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as the intended or direct way.
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r2.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: " {قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل} [القصص: 22] قال: قصد السبيل

TAB-FULL:v18p205/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r3.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as the straight path.
TAB-FULL:v18p205/r3.anchor: عن الحسن: " {عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل} [القصص: 22] قال: الطريق المستقيم

SULAMI:v2p102#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p102#3/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p102#3/r1.claim: Moses faced Midian with his body and faced God with his heart, seeking guidance; God honored him with speech, and whoever wholly turns to God reaches his hoped-for end.
SULAMI:v2p102#3/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : توجه بوجهه إلى ناحية مدين وتوجه بقلبه إلى ربه

SULAMI:v2p102#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p102#3/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الحراز
SULAMI:v2p102#3/r2.claim: The lights of discernment and divine conversation led Moses to encounter Shuʿayb; that meeting began his blessings.
SULAMI:v2p102#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الحراز حملته أنوار الفراسة وتدابير المكالمة فيه فصادف بها شعيبا

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.claim: This episode recounts Moses’ flight from Egypt after killing the Egyptian, his arrival in Midian, and his marriage there to an unnamed elder’s daughter.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r1.anchor: يذكر فيه خروجه من مصر إلى مدين عقيب قتله القبطي خوفا من فرعون

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r2.speaker: روايات أئمة أهل البيت وبعض روايات أهل السنة
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r2.claim: Some Imami reports and some Sunni reports identify the unnamed elder whom Moses later marries into as the prophet Shuʿayb.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r2.anchor: لكن تذكر روايات أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام وبعض روايات أهل السنة أنه هو شعيب النبي

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r3.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r3.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses تلقاء as facing or opposite; the phrase تلقاء نفسه means acting from one’s own impulse.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r3.anchor: قال في المجمع تلقاء الشيء حذاؤه، ويقال فعل ذلك من تلقاء نفسه

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r4.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r4.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains سواء السبيل as the middle of the road.

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r5.speaker: مراصد الاطلاع
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r5.claim: Marāṣid al-Iṭṭilāʿ locates Midian opposite Tabuk on the Red Sea, six stages away, larger than Tabuk, and containing the well where Moses watered Shuʿayb’s flock.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r5.anchor: ومدين - على ما في مراصد الاطلاع - مدينة قوم شعيب وهي تجاه تبوك

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r6.claim: Midian is said to be an eight-day journey from Egypt and outside Pharaoh’s jurisdiction, which explains Moses’ choice of destination.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r6.anchor: ويقال إنه كان بينهما وبين مصر مسيرة ثمان وكانت خارجة من سلطان فرعون

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r7.claim: Moses turned toward Midian and hoped God would guide him along the road’s middle so he would not stray from it.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r7.anchor: قال أرجو من ربي أن يهديني وسط الطريق فلا أضل بالعدول عنه

TABATABAI:28:22-24/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r8.claim: The context implies Moses was heading to Midian without knowing the route and therefore hoped God would guide him.
TABATABAI:28:22-24/r8.anchor: كان قاصدا لمدين وهو لا يعرف الطريق الموصلة إليها فترجى أن يهديه ربه

TABATABAI:28:22-28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r1.claim: Moses closely monitored his actions, pursuing even natural needs only for God’s approval and struggle in His cause; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī infers this from his sequence of prayers and commitments.
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r1.anchor: ويظهر منه أنه عليه السلام كان ذا مراقبة شديدة في أعماله فلا يأتي بعمل

TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.claim: God answered Moses’ three prayers: he was safe from his pursuers, reached the road to Midian, and received provision through the watering reward, ten years’ livelihood, and a wife.
TABATABAI:28:22-28/r8.anchor: وعند ذلك تمت استجابته تعالى لموسى عليه السلام أدعيته الثلاثة

TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.claim: A report from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq recounts Moses’ exhausting flight to Midian, where he drew water for two young women unable to jostle with the men; they brought him to their father.
TABATABAI:28:22-28#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث طويل وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى

FARRA:v2p304/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p304/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p304/r1.claim: سواء السبيل is the road to Midian, whose route Moses did not know.
FARRA:v2p304/r1.anchor: وقوله (أن يهديني سواء السبيل) : الطريق إلى مدين ولم يكن هاديا لطريقها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r1.claim: Tilqāʾ means toward or facing Midian; it derives from liqāʾ with an added tāʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r1.anchor: تلقاء مدين} أي تجاه مدين ونحوها. وأصله:

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses tilqāʾ in the sense of meeting or facing someone, supporting its relation to liqāʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: فاليوم قصر عن تلقائه الأمل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p331#2/r3.claim: Sawāʾ al-sabīl means the straight or intended course.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r1.claim: Tawajjaha means that Moses set out toward Midian.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r1.anchor: قصد بوجهه { تلقاء مدين } نحوها { قال عسى ربي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r2.claim: Moses asked God to guide him to the right road because he did not know the route.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:22-24/r2.anchor: قصد الطريق، وذلك أنه لم يكن يعرف الطريق

ELMALILI:28:22/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:22/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:22/r1.claim: Midian is the homeland of the prophet Shuayb, as explained earlier.
ELMALILI:28:22/r1.anchor: Yukarılarda geçtiği üzere Şuayb aleyhisselâm’ın memleketi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r1.claim: Midian was an ancient city near Maʿan, north of the Gulf of Aqaba, and about an eight-day walk from Egypt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r1.anchor: Medyen, Akabe körfezinin kuzeyindeki Maan yakınlarında, Mısır’a yaya yürüyüşü ile sekiz günlük mesafede bulunan eski bir şehirdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.claim: Because Midian's people were Arab and close to the Israelites in ethnicity and language, it is historically plausible that they helped Moses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:22/r2.anchor: Buranın halkı Arap asıllı olduğu için Hz. Mûsâ’nın soyundan olan İbrânîler’e hem ırk hem de dil bakımından yakındılar, dolayısıyla ona yardım etmiş olmaları tarihen mümkündür

BAQILLANI:v1p25/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r1.claim: The first Muslims accepted the Qur'an's proof from insight rather than imitation or a referral to all eloquent speakers; people with sharper understanding accepted sooner.
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r1.anchor: ونعلم أن السابقين الأولين إلى الإسلام لم يقلدوه إنما دخلوا على بصيرة

BAQILLANI:v1p25/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r2.claim: People differ in how quickly they grasp the proof: foreigners must infer Arab incapacity, and intermediate speakers must infer the limits of the most eloquent experts.
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r2.anchor: لأن الأعجمي لا يعلم أنه معجز إلا بأن يعلم عجز العرب عنه وهو يحتاج في معرفة ذلك إلى أمور

BAQILLANI:v1p25/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r3.claim: Expertise in poetry, sermons, or letters alone is insufficient; immediate recognition requires complete knowledge of rhetorical forms and eloquent speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r3.anchor: فلا تكون الحجة قائمة على المختص ببعض هذه العلوم بانفرادها دون تحققه لعجز البارع في هذه العلوم كلها عنه

BAQILLANI:v1p25/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r4.claim: A fully accomplished rhetor recognizes the Qur'an's inimitability on hearing it; otherwise one would wrongly imply that the Prophet learned this only after testing the Arabs.
BAQILLANI:v1p25/r4.anchor: فأما من كان متناهيا في معرفة وجوه الخطاب وطرق البلاغة والفنون التي يمكن فيها إظهار الفصاحة فهو متى سمع القرآن عرف إعجازه

BURHAN:v2p330/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p330/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p330/r1.claim: An interrogative with an imperfect can deny that an act occurs at all, as in “shall we force it upon you?”; it can also warn someone against taking a dangerous course.
BURHAN:v2p330/r1.anchor: وفيه دخول الاستفهام على المضارع فإذا قلت أتفعل أو أأنت تفعل احتمل وجهين أحدهما إنكار وجود الفعل

BURHAN:v2p330/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p330/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p330/r2.claim: Fronting the object redirects the censure to whether the agent is fit to perform the act, as in “shall I take a patron other than God?”
BURHAN:v2p330/r2.anchor: والثاني قولك لمن يركب الخطر أتذهب في غير طريق انظر لنفسك واستبصر فإذا قدمت المفعول توجه الإنكار إلى كونه بمثابة أن يوقع به مثل ذلك الفعل

BURHAN:v2p330/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p330/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p330/r3.claim: A rejecting question can insinuate that the addressee claimed or committed the rejected thing, accusing them of a false assertion explicitly or by implication.
BURHAN:v2p330/r3.anchor: الثاني قد يصحب الإنكار التكذيب للتعريض بأن المخاطب ادعاه وقصد تكذيبه

BURHAN:v2p330/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p330/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p330/r4.claim: The author distinguishes invalidating rejection, where the claimed act is unreal and its claimant false, from genuine rebuke, where the act occurred but its agent is blameworthy.
BURHAN:v2p330/r4.anchor: والحاصل ان الانكار قسمان ابطالي وحقيقي فالابطالي ان يكون ما بعدها غير واقع ومدعيه كاذب

DAMGHANI:v1p429/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p429/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p429/r5.claim: مدين is the town of Shuayb, including the destination in Moses' journey.
DAMGHANI:v1p429/r5.anchor: الثالث : مدين قرية شعيب . قوله سبحانه فى سورة الأعراف وهود والعنكبوت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r1.claim: In ordinary Arabic, sabīl means a road; context can also make it figurative.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r1.anchor: السبيل في اللغة الطريق ويستعار في مواضع تدل عليها القرينة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r2.claim: Exegetes use sabīl for obedience, as in spending and fighting in God's cause.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r3.claim: Exegetes use sabīl for ability or means to reach the pilgrimage obligation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r4.claim: Exegetes use sabīl for an exit or way out.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r5.claim: Exegetes use sabīl for a course or way, as in the expression “an evil way.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r6.claim: In 4:34 it means pretexts: after wives obey, do not seek grounds against them or demand that they love you.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r7.claim: Sabīl can mean religion, as in following believers, taking an intermediate way, or calling to the Lord's way.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r8.claim: It can mean a road or path; this verse asks God to guide Moses to the right path.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r9.claim: It can mean an argument or authority, including God's not granting disbelievers authority over believers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r10.claim: It can mean aggression or liability: the text places liability on those who wrong people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r10.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r11.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r11.claim: It can mean sin or liability, as when the text denies grounds for blame against the sick and benefactors.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p364/r11.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السبيل في القرآن على أحد عشر وجها

THALABI:v7p242/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p242/r15.claim: Tiqāʾ Madian means toward and intending Midian, beyond Pharaoh's authority; one says two houses are tiqāʾ when they face each other, and the word comes from liqāʾ.
THALABI:v7p242/r15.anchor: أي نحوها وقصدها ماضيا لها، خارجا عن سلطان فرعون، يقال: داره تلقاء دار فلان إذا كانت محاذيتها، وأصله من اللقاء،

THALABI:v7p242/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p242/r16.claim: Madyan is not declined because it is the name of a known town.
THALABI:v7p242/r16.anchor: ولم تصرف مدين لأنها اسم بلدة معروفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses left without knowing which direction to take, and God prepared the way to Midian for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ذكر أنه خرج على وجهه {خائفا يترقب} ما يدري أي وجه يسلك، فهيأ الله له الطريق إلى مدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses the phrase as toward Midian, deriving it from اللقاء with an added tāʾ; he cites poetry where تلقائك means meeting you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال ابن قتيبة: أي تجاه مدين ونحوها، وأصله: اللقاء، زيدت فيه التاء، وأنشد: فاليوم قصر عن تلقائك الأمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq says Moses took the road that would lead him to Midian.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: معنى: {تلقاء مدين} أي: سلك في الطريق التي يلقى مدين فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r4.claim: They say Moses traveled from Egypt to Midian without provisions, shoes, or a mount; the journey was eight days.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق، وغيره: خرج موسى من مصر إلى مدين بغير زاد، ولا حذاء ولا ظهر، وبينهما مسيرة ثمانية أيام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses did not know the route and relied on his good opinion of God when asking to be guided to the right way.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r5.anchor: [قال ابن عباس:] (¬6) وليس له بالطريق علم إلا حسن ظنه بربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r6.claim: Muqatil says Moses set out without a guide, feared losing the road, and asked God to guide him toward Midian.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: توجه نحو مدين بغير دليل، وخشي أن يضل الطريق فقال: عسى ربي يرشدني قصد الطريق إلى مدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r7.claim: The phrase means the direct course of the road, maintaining straightness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r7.anchor: ومعنى {سواء السبيل}: قصد السبيل في الاستواء

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r3.claim: “Toward Midian” means in the direction of Midian.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r4.claim: Qatāda identifies Midian as a watering place inhabited by Shuʿayb’s people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: ومدين ماء كان عليه قوم شعيب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r5.claim: Moses’ hope that God guide him means that God direct him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r5.anchor: {قال عسى ربي أن يهديني} [القصص: 22] أن يرشدني.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r6.speaker: قتادة والسدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r6.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī take the straight way as the direct road to Midian; Moses did not know where to go or how to find it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r6.anchor: {سواء السبيل} [القصص: 22] قال قتادة والسدي، يعني: قصد الطريق إلى مدين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r7.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r7.claim: Mujāhid specifies that the straight way is the route to Midian.

QASHANI:28:20-22/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:20-22/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:20-22/r5.claim: When he turns toward Midian, the station of spirit, strong will lets hope overcome fear as he seeks true guidance through spiritual lights and manifestations of the attributes on the path of unity and wayfaring in God.
QASHANI:28:20-22/r5.anchor: غلب رجاؤه على الخوف لقوة الإرادة وطلب الهداية الحقانية بالأنوار الروحية

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r7.claim: Moses set out toward Midian without having chosen that destination, went in reliance on divine opening, and turned his heart to God for guidance to the best way.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r7.anchor: توجه بنفسه تلقاء مدين من غير قصد إلى مدين أو غيره ، بل خرج على الفتوح ، توجه بقلبه إلى ربه

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

ITQAN:v2p410/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p410/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p410/r18.claim: Huda can mean showing or directing someone to the right way.

DAMGHANI:v1p472/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r11.claim: Hudā can mean the right way or guidance to the road; the source also points to examples in Sād and Umm al-Kitāb.
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r11.anchor: السابع الهدى الرشد قوله سبحانه في سورة القصص عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r2.claim: Hudā can mean guidance or direction to the right path.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p627/r2.anchor: والسادس : الإرشاد . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r1.claim: The root meaning of هدى is to guide; in the cited prayers it means أرشدنا, guide us.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r1.anchor: أصل هدى أرشد، كقوله: عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

MAJAZ:v2p100/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p100/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p100/r2.claim: Tilqāʾa Madyan means toward Midian. Madyan is indeclinable because it is a feminine name; tilqāʾ also means facing or toward.
MAJAZ:v2p100/r2.anchor: «ولما توجه تلقاء مدين» (22) مجازه: نحو مدين ولا تنصرف مدين لأنها اسم مؤنثة

MAJAZ:v2p100/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p100/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p100/r3.claim: Sawāʾ al-sabīl means the middle or direct course of the road; an unnamed poet’s line uses sawāʾ, which is open and long.
MAJAZ:v2p100/r3.anchor: «سواء السبيل» (22) مجازه قصد السبيل ووسطه قال: حتى أغيب فى سواء الملحد

NAHHAS:v3p232/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r20.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p232/r20.claim: Moses took the road leading toward Midian; sawāʾ al-sabīl means the straight or direct road.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r20.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أي سلك الطريق الذي هو تلقاء مدين

NAHHAS:v3p232/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p232/r21.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p232/r21.claim: Abū Isḥāq says Midian does not decline because it is a place name.
NAHHAS:v3p232/r21.anchor: ولم ينصرف مدين لأنه اسم للبقعة

ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r2.claim: Madyan was Shuayb's people's watering place, said to be eight days from Egypt, about the distance between Basra and Kufa.
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r2.anchor: ماء كان لقوم شعيب يقال إن بينه وبين مصر

ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r3.claim: Moses took the road leading toward Madyan.
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r3.anchor: سلك في الطريق التي تلقاء مدين فيها

ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r4.claim: سبيل is a road; سواء السبيل means the straight, direct course.
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r4.anchor: سواء السبيل قصد الطريق في الاستواء

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.claim: Qasas retains the speaker's yāʾ in yahdīnī because Moses flees Pharaoh in fear and turns wholly to God; Kahf's less urgent prayer omits it, using the kasra instead.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r1.anchor: الخوف يستدعي أن يلصق الإنسان بمن يحميه ويلقي بنفسه كلها عليه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.claim: In Qasas, 'Lord' precedes the guidance verb because the fearful speaker first seeks his protector; Kahf foregrounds guidance because its context asks for right direction amid differing views.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r2.anchor: قدم (الرب) على فعل الهداية لأنه هو الملجأ فقال

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.claim: The yāʾ pronoun occurs more often in Qasas, and guidance is mentioned twelve times there against five in Kahf; the greater recurrence supports the fuller form in Qasas.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r3.anchor: ثم لننظر من ناحية أخرى فإن ياء الضمير تكرر في (القصص) أكثر مما في الكهف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.claim: Qasas tells Moses' story at length, while the Kahf prayer occurs briefly within the sleepers' story; Samarrai links the longer account to the longer verb form and the concise account to deletion.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r4.anchor: مقام التبسط والتطويل في (القصص) في قصة موسى أكثر بكثير مما ورد في (الكهف)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.claim: As another example of retaining or omitting the first-person yā, he contrasts “may guide me” in 18:24 with the explicit yā in 28:22.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r13.anchor: ومن ذلك: أي ذِكْرُ ياءِ المتكلم أو حذفها قوله تعالى: {وَقُلْ عسى أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هاذا رَشَداً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.claim: The reform exception fits the Queen of Sheba, who left sun-worship and submitted to God; Moses was already a believer, and his confession of wrong concerned killing the Egyptian, not a change from disbelief.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.anchor: فإنها ظلمت نفسها بكفرها وسجودِها للشمس من دون الله، ثم بدّلت حُسْناً بعد سوء، فأسلمتْ لله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.claim: Al-Qasas uses expressions of hope in ten places, while al-Naml has only two; the author says hope marks al-Qasas and certainty marks al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.anchor: الترجي من سمات سورة القصص، والقطع من سمات سورة النمل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.claim: Of twelve disputed possessive yāʾs, Nafi opens all except معي ردءا, which he leaves quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا قوله ﴿ معي ردءا ﴾ فإنه أسكنها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr open nine listed possessive yāʾs and leave quiescent إني أريد, ستجدني إن شاء الله, and معي ردءا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.anchor: وفتح ابن كثير تسع آيات منهن وأسكن ﴿ إني أريد ﴾ و ﴿ ستجدني إن شاء الله ﴾

NASHR:v2p342/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r7.speaker: يعقوب والكوفيون
NASHR:v2p342/r7.claim: Yaʿqūb and the Kufans make the yāʾ still in both occurrences of لعلي.
NASHR:v2p342/r7.anchor: لعلي موضعان أسكنها فيهما يعقوب، والكوفيون،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r3.claim: Tijāha Midian means heading toward it; a house is said to be tilqāʾ another when it faces it, from the root of meeting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r3.anchor: أي: قصد نحوها ماضيا إليها، يقال: داره تلقاء دار فلان، إذا كانت محاذيتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Moses took the road that faces Midian.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: يعني سلك الطريق الذي تلقاء مدين فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r5.claim: Midian was a son of Abraham, and the town was named after him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r5.anchor: ومدين هو مدين بن إبراهيم، سميت البلدة باسمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r6.claim: Moses fled without a mount, shoes, or provisions; Midian was eight days’ journey from Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r6.anchor: وكان موسى قد خرج خائفا بلا ظهر ولا حذاء ولا زاد، وكانت مدين على مسيرة ثمانية أيام من مصر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r7.claim: Moses asked for guidance to the route to Midian because he had not known the way there; an angel carrying a staff then led him to it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r7.anchor: أي: قصد الطريق إلى مدين، قال ذلك لأنه لم يكن يعرف الطريق إليها قبل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r8.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r8.claim: The exegetes say Moses had only leaves and greens to eat, saw their greenness in his belly, and wore through his soles before reaching Midian.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r8.anchor: قال المفسرون: خرج موسى من مصر ولم يكن له طعام إلا ورق الشجر والبقل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this journey was Moses’ first trial from God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وهو أول ابتلاء من الله عز وجل لموسى عليه السلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r2.claim: Midian is opposite him, a village named for Midian son of Abraham and associated with Shuʿayb; it was outside Pharaoh's realm, eight days from Egypt.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r2.anchor: قبالة مدين قرية شعيب، سميت باسم مدين بن إبراهيم عليهم الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r3.claim: Trusting God and expecting good, Moses chose the middle of three routes without knowing the way; pursuers came after him and took the other two.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r3.anchor: وكان لا يعرف الطريق فعن له ثلاث طرق فأخذ في أوسطها وجاء الطلاب عقيبه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.claim: God answers by directing Moses toward Midian along the main road; his pursuers miss him because they assume a fugitive would use side routes or cross-country paths.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.anchor: فاستجاب الله له فوفقه لسلوك الطريق الأعظم نحو مدين , فكان ذلك سبب نجاته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r5.claim: Moses turns his face toward Midian and sets out intending to reach it, while directing his heart toward God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r5.anchor: مدينة نبي الله شعيب عليه الصلاة والسللام متوجها بقلبه إلى ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r6.claim: ʿAsā here means fitting, worthy, and assuredly possible.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r7.claim: Moses places Rabb first because his care and watchfulness toward God are especially strong.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r7.anchor: ولما كانت عنايته بالله أتم لما له من عظيم المراقبة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r8.claim: The proper middle of the road is the route God will show him without deviation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r8.anchor: أي عدل ووسط { السبيل * } وهو الطريق الذي يطلعه عليها من غير اعوجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r3.claim: Moses took a well-traveled route toward Midian, hoped God would guide him to the right way, and God guided him in this life and the next, making him a guide who was himself guided.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r3.anchor: أخذ طريقا سالكا مهيعا فرح بذلك

JISHUMI:v8p5484/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r4.claim: Tilqāʾ means toward or opposite; related phrases describe acting independently or a house facing another, from the root liqāʾ.
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r4.anchor: وتلقاءه: حذاءه، ويقال: فعله من تلقاء نفسه، وداره تلقاء دار فلان

JISHUMI:v8p5484/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r5.claim: Tawajjuh means turning toward something with one's face.

JISHUMI:v8p5484/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r11.claim: Madyan is diptote because it is a town name; an unattributed poem is cited in illustration.
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r11.anchor: (مدين) لا ينصرف؛ لأنه اسم بلدة، قال الشاعر: رهبان مدين لو رأوك تنزلوا

MUQATIL:28:20-23/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r5.claim: Moses travelled from Egypt to Midian without a guide in ten days.
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r5.anchor: فسار من مصر إلى مدين في عشرة أيام بغير دليل

MUQATIL:28:20-23/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r6.claim: Without a guide, Moses feared losing the route and asked God to guide him to the straight road to Midian, which he reached.
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r6.anchor: بغير دليل خشى أن يضل الطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r9.claim: Moses fled alone, afraid and without provisions, comfort, or shoes, toward Midian because of his kinship with its people; seeing his ignorance of the route and need, he entrusted himself to God for guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r9.anchor: لما خرج موسى عليه السلام فارا بنفسه منفردا خائفا، لا شيء معه من زاد ولا راحة ولا حذاء نحو مدين

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r10.speaker: أبو مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r10.claim: Abu Malik says Pharaoh sent searchers to the road passes, where Moses would be lost; an angel on horseback with a spear guided him and, it is said, gave him his staff.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r10.anchor: قال أبو مالك: وكان فرعون وجه في طلبه وقال لهم: اطلبوه في ثنيات الطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r11.claim: Another account says Moses took the staff in Midian for shepherding; the author says this account is more common and sounder.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r11.anchor: ويروى أن عصاه إنما أخذها لرعي الغنم من مدين. وهو أكثر وأصح

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r12.speaker: مقاتل والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r12.claim: Muqatil and al-Suddi say God sent Gabriel to Moses; the author leaves the truth to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل والسدي: إن الله بعث إليه جبريل فالله أعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r13.speaker: ابن جبير والناس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r13.claim: Ibn Jubayr and others say the journey from Egypt to Midian took eight days, and Midian was ruled by someone other than Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r13.anchor: وبين مدين ومصر ثمانية أيام قاله ابن جبير والناس. وكان ملك مدين لغير فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r14.speaker: أبو مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r14.claim: A report says Moses lived on leaves and reached Midian after the soles of his feet wore away.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r14.anchor: قلت: روي أنه كان يتقوت ورق الشجر، وما وصل حتى سقط خف قدميه
